ledger.x: 1046: King Wu founds the Zhou at Fenghao.
c. 1045: Cai enfeoffed. 'King Wu of Zhou granted titles and territories to his younger brothers'; infobox 'Established: c. 1045 bce'.

wars.name: Zhou–Chu War (King Zhao's southern campaigns)
wars.outcome: 'a successful southern campaign in the Han River region, in the 16th year of King Zhao's reign'; 'A second campaign in the same area three years later ended with King Zhao losing his armies and his own life'; 'until the disastrous Zhou–Chu War in 977 BC'.

wars.name: Battle of Mount Li and the fall of Haojing
wars.outcome: The Quanrong and the Marquis of Shen 'defeated King You's royal forces at the Battle of Mount Li in 771 BC' and 'sacked the Zhou capital Fenghao'; the court moved to Luoyi; the Western Zhou ended.

certainty.note: A Bronze Age kingdom of fiefs: no fixed frontiers anywhere; the northern and western edges (Xianyun, Quanrong, Guifang) and the Han valley are the softest.
